actions.justification: Mandatory first action - assess vital signs to establish baseline and confirm hemodynamic stability in this patient with acute gout flare, atrial fibrillation, and hypertension on warfarin.

Assess the acute right knee pain and swelling in detail - characterize onset, severity, prior gout history, and current anticoagulation status to guide appropriate gout management while considering warfarin interactions.

Patient has atrial fibrillation and hypertension; cardiovascular assessment is important to evaluate rate control and hemodynamic stability, especially since medications used for gout (NSAIDs, colchicine) may interact with warfarin or affect cardiovascular function.
Assess overall clinical condition of the patient with acute gout flare, including pain severity, functional status, and appearance to guide management decisions.
Evaluate hydration status as adequate hydration is important in gout flare management and affects uric acid excretion; also relevant given patient is on warfarin.
Rule out septic arthritis, which is a critical differential diagnosis for acute monoarthritis with warmth and swelling — requires urgent exclusion before treating as gout.

Patient presents with acute right knee pain and swelling — direct musculoskeletal assessment is essential to characterize the joint involvement, assess for warmth/erythema/effusion, and support the working diagnosis of acute gout flare.
Baseline mental status assessment is important given the patient's age, hypertension, and atrial fibrillation, and to ensure safe administration of analgesics/anti-inflammatory agents.
Quantify pain severity to guide analgesic selection and monitor response to treatment in this acute gout flare. Critical given warfarin use limits NSAID options.
Patient is on warfarin for AF with hypertension — assess renal and hepatic function as these affect gout medication choices (colchicine, NSAIDs, steroids) and warfarin metabolism.
Patient has AF and hypertension with elevated BP (148/86); brief neurological assessment to rule out concurrent neurological events before proceeding with treatment.

Perform a focused assessment of the patient with acute right knee pain/swelling on warfarin, evaluating joint characteristics (warmth, erythema, effusion, range of motion) to confirm working diagnosis of acute gout flare and assess severity.
Assess skin over the affected knee for erythema, warmth, and other findings to differentiate gout from septic arthritis or cellulitis, which is critical in this anticoagulated patient.

Assess abdominal status to evaluate for any secondary contributors and ensure no contraindications to planned treatments (e.g., NSAIDs, colchicine) given the patient's comorbidities including AF on warfarin and hypertension.

Assess renal function before initiating treatment for acute gout flare; critical given warfarin use and comorbidities (hypertension, AF). eGFR guides safe use of NSAIDs, colchicine dosing, and uricosuric agents.
Monitor renal perfusion and function in this patient with hypertension and gout flare; urine output assessment complements eGFR to guide treatment safety.

Rheumatology or internal medicine consultation indicated for acute gout management in a complex patient on warfarin (drug interaction risk with NSAIDs/colchicine) and with atrial fibrillation and hypertension.

Establishing IV access is important for this patient on warfarin with acute gout flare — allows IV medication administration if needed and facilitates blood draws for labs including INR monitoring given warfarin use.
Complete the respiratory assessment as part of thorough initial evaluation, especially relevant given atrial fibrillation comorbidity which can have respiratory implications.

Patient has severe acute gout flare on warfarin for atrial fibrillation requiring inpatient management for pain control, joint aspiration/workup, INR monitoring, and careful medication selection (NSAIDs contraindicated with warfarin; colchicine dose adjustment needed). Ward admission is appropriate given stable vitals but complex comorbidity profile.

Patient has acute gout flare on warfarin for atrial fibrillation requiring careful medication management (NSAIDs contraindicated with anticoagulation, colchicine dose adjustment needed, steroids may be preferred). Hospital admission allows INR monitoring, pain management, and safe treatment initiation under specialist supervision.
